title: rwb-decision next action: the answer shape of the rule-catalog and latest-state-change reads, and their not-found and malformed-parameter messages, are not specified
source: RWB-P2-E2035-CON (section 12.2, 12.8 and the two consumed rows of the call matrix); RWB-P3-E2042-CON (the RuleCatalog.row operation and the version-state vocabulary); TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1, T3.2 and appendix T-A.1; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.3 and A2.7; Legacy RWB-E2-035 sections 8, 11, 12 and 14
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 3 and 4; section 8 Business rule BR1; section 11 Data; section 12.1 and 12.8 Contract; section 14 Validation and messages
description: The two shapes this story provides are declared by their consumers, not by the registry's own technical specification. RWB-P2-E2035-CON names rule-catalog actions as action_text, owner_role, timer_spec and outputs only, while the legacy row also carries rule_version, to_state and drools_rule_name and the target row carries package_version_id; no source says whether the answer also carries the package code, the version label, the version state and an in-force flag, which this slice adds so that AC2 and AC5 can be asserted. The decision-log filter adds latestStateChange and no source fixes its answer fields beyond rule ID and rule version, nor whether an empty answer is a 200 with a flag or a 404. No source fixes the message for a rule row or version label that does not exist, or for an absent packageVersion, and TSD P7 T-A.1 lists eight operations, none of which is the catalogue read.
evidence: RWB-P2-E2035-CON lists GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion= with 'action_text, owner_role, timer_spec and outputs of the firing rule' and GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId=&latestStateChange=true with 'The latest state change of a case: rule ID and rule version'; TSD P7 T-A.1 lists API-P7-001 to API-P7-008 only; FSD P7 A2.3 and A2.7 define the entry fields DF-DEC-004 and DF-DEC-005 and the rule tables but no read contract; Legacy RWB-E2-035 section 12 declares RuleCatalog.row returning a RuleRow with rule_version, to_state and drools_rule_name and section 14 defines no message for an unknown rule row.
area: rwb-decision catalogue and ledger read contract
proposed: Fix both answer schemas in the API specification and in the RWB-P3-E2042-CON catalogue section: the row answer carries packageCode, packageVersion, versionState, inForce, ruleId, ruleVersion, actionText, ownerRole, timerSpec, toState, droolsRuleName and outputs; the latest-state-change answer carries entryId, ruleId, ruleVersion, decidedAt and missing, and is 200 with missing true when the case has none. Add the 404 and 422 entries of MSG-P3-027 and MSG-GEN-001 to the message catalogue for these two reads.

title: The valid-from date of package version RES-2026.12 is 2026-12-15 in the registry stories and before 11 December 2026 in the legacy key every test of this story reads
source: RWB-P7-E2042-APP (the three Epic 2 versions valid from 2026-12-15); RWB-P3-E2035-APP (the version in force per environment read from the registry on every evaluation); Legacy RWB-E2-035 background and acceptance criteria AC1 to AC12 (RES-2026.12 in force on 11 to 30 December 2026)
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 Background; section 12.8 Contract fakes; section 16 Test cases
description: The registry story pins the three Epic 2 package versions, RESTRUCTURE among them, to a valid-from date of 2026-12-15, copied from the legacy assumption of RWB-E2-042. The legacy key RWB-E2-035 evaluates and reads RES-2026.12 from 11 December 2026 and its criteria move cases on 11, 14 and 30 December 2026 and on 5 January 2027, all of which need that version in force. One of the two dates is wrong, and the fixtures of this story's fourteen test cases depend on which one.
evidence: RWB-P7-E2042-APP section 3 reads 'all valid from 2026-12-15 (the valid-from date is the legacy assumption and is copied unchanged)'; RWB-E2-035 section 7 AC1 and AC2 move case RW-2026-000401 by R-RES-04 of RES-2026.12 on 11 December 2026 and AC7 reads a move on 30 December 2026 with the same version; RWB-P3-E2035-APP reads the version in force from the rwb-decision registry on every evaluation with no lock file.
proposed: Reconcile one valid-from date for RES-2026.12 before the wave-2 fixture is frozen: either move the registry valid-from to 2026-12-01, which the ITG harness and RWB-P3-E2035-APP already use, or re-date the legacy criteria. Until then the fixtures of this story keep the legacy reading.

title: rwb-decision next action: no source enumerates the decision codes or final calls that count as a state change for the latestStateChange filter
source: TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-003 and T3.2; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.3; Legacy RWB-E2-035 sections 4, 8 and 12
section: Section 8 Business rule BR5; section 9 State transitions; section 12.1 Contract; section 13 Components
description: The fill of a case with no next action asks for the latest state change of the case and needs the rule ID and rule version that moved it. The ledger entry holds DF-DEC-003 decision_code on list LOV-DECISION and DF-DEC-012 final_call as free text, and LOV-DECISION is named in the TSD but never enumerated in T3.2, which lists LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-PRODUCT only. No source says whether a state change is identified by a decision code, by a final call such as CASE_TRANSFERRED or OWNER_ASSIGNED, or simply by the entry carrying a rule ID and a rule version.
evidence: TSD P7 T3.1 DF-DEC-003 reads 'decision_code | LOV | varchar(8) | Yes | LOV-DECISION' and DF-DEC-012 reads 'final_call | TEXT | varchar(40) | Yes'; TSD P7 T3.2 enumerates four lists and LOV-DECISION is not one of them; FSD P7 A2.3 gives the entry the rule ID, rule version and inputs and does not classify the entries; Legacy RWB-E2-035 section 12 asks DecisionLogQuery.latestStateChange for a RuleRef only.
proposed: Publish LOV-DECISION in the reference-data load with the state-change codes marked, and let the filter read the mark rather than a list of codes in code; until then the read takes the newest entry of the case that carries a rule ID and a rule version.

title: rwb-decision next action: rule_row.timer_spec has no list of values, and two legacy specs are outside the four shapes the legacy rule enumerates
source: Legacy RWB-E2-035 business rule BR3, BR4 and the background of section 7; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.7
section: Section 4 Flow step 5; section 7 Background and AC3; section 8 Business rule BR3; section 17 Guardrails
description: Legacy BR3 enumerates four timer shapes — 'n working days', 'n days' with a label before it, 'same day' or 'immediate', and 'next working day' — and legacy BR4 sends every other value, including 'None', to the service levels and timers table of the case side. The legacy background and criteria also use 'payment due 30 days' and 'deadline driven', which fit neither BR3 nor cleanly BR4, and the target column carries no list. This story returns the string as stored and computes nothing, so the question it cannot answer is how the caller parses those two values.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-035 BR3 enumerates the four shapes and BR4 names 'None' as the case where the table is read; the background of section 7 gives R-SET-13 the timer 'payment due 30 days' and AC6 gives R-DEV-05 the timer 'deadline driven'; TSD P7 T3.1 and FSD P7 A2.7 describe the rule tables without a timer list or a timer column definition.
proposed: Publish the timer spec shapes as a list of values with their parsing rule in the reference data of rwb-case and extend it with the two legacy values, so the caller parses data and the registry returns a string.

title: The published catalogue path shows packageVersion as an optional query parameter and no source says what an absent value answers
source: RWB-P2-E2035-CON section 12.2 and the exception X3; RWB-P3-E2042-CON; Legacy RWB-E2-035 section 12
section: Section 5 Exception path X1; section 8 Business rule BR7; section 12.1 Contract
description: The path of the consumed operation is written as GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion= with the value left empty, which reads as optional, while the legacy operation is called with both a rule ID and a package version and the legacy rule states that a later version never rewrites an action already set. No source says whether an absent packageVersion means the version in force on the business date or a refusal. The business date a default would need is itself not a field of the operation.
evidence: RWB-P2-E2035-CON lists 'GET | /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion=' and its exception X3 refuses a resolve called without a rule ID, a package version or a business date with MSG-GEN-001; RWB-P3-E2042-CON names the operation RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion); Legacy RWB-E2-035 section 12 shows both parameters and BR10 states that a later version does not rewrite an action already set.
proposed: Mark packageVersion required in the API specification and keep the refusal of MSG-GEN-001, so no caller is ever answered from a version in force that the case was not moved under.

title: A secondary registry slice carries no build dependency while the DP rows add seven platform contracts and four published contracts
source: Template and Rules v1 section R5.4 and R5.7; RWB-P2-E2035-CON; RWB-P7-E1073-APP; RWB-P7-E2042-APP
description: The WP fixes Depends on (build) as empty and Contract dependencies as RWB-P2-E2035-CON only. The twelve DP rows this key applies add H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and C RWB-P2-E2035-CON, RWB-P3-E2042-CON, RWB-P7-E1073-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON, plus the rows of RWB-P7-E1073-APP and RWB-P7-E1008-APP that this story reads. No source says which of them block the start of a secondary slice.
evidence: The WP line for RWB-P7-E2035-APP reads H: [] and C: [RWB-P2-E2035-CON]; Template and Rules R5.4 makes H the only blocking class and R5.7 rule 8 makes Ready to start Day 1 when the only H dependencies are contracts; RWB-P7-E1073-APP and RWB-P7-E1008-APP are wave-1 stories of the same service whose rows this story reads.
proposed: Record in the build sequence that a secondary slice builds against the platform contracts and the published fakes and reads the same service's wave-1 rows through its own schema, so the lane depth stays inside the limit of R5.7 rule 5.

title: The per-service database login name of rwb-decision is named in no source
source: Architecture v5 service table; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T1; Template and Rules v1 section R4; the Ownership Map
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Every service carries one login of its own (DP-02) and no document names it. The story therefore refers to the rwb-decision login and never to the shared monolith login, and the name has to be set in the platform DB story before the deployment.
evidence: The TSD P7 T1 describes one service with one repository and one front end and names no login; Architecture v5 slide 8 states one ACE PostgreSQL server with 19 Recovery schemas, one login and connection pool each, and no login name; the Ownership Map assigns the schema and the tables, not the credentials.
proposed: Fix the login name in RWB-PLT-DB and in the secret store, with the migration role and the application role kept apart, and reference it from every P7 story.
